source fidelity, answer uniqueness, semantic distinctness, commercial practice value, plausible distractors and explanation correctness

decisions.rationale: Tier B PASS. Q180 ends at GNSS-disabled hover stability and Q085 tests generic VRS prevention during descent. C001 is the source-explicit GNSS-disabled landing sequence that combines stabilized hover, throttle descent, and fine elevator/aileron input through touchdown, changing both flight phase and required control sequence.

The source explicitly requires a multirotor pilot to stop rotor rotation with the controller after touchdown. Q183 is helicopter-specific and tests when a person may approach the aircraft, not the pilot shutdown action. Aircraft applicability and answer-defining action differ.

The source explicitly requires anticipating the helicopter's tail-rotor-induced takeoff tilt direction from rotor rotation direction. Q068 concerns counter-torque/yaw function and Q182 concerns sufficient rotor RPM; neither tests the pre-liftoff lateral-tilt anticipation step.

Tier B PASS. Q132 recognizes helicopter ground effect and Q325 covers landing-phase avoidance of lingering in ground effect. C004 tests the separate takeoff-phase action to climb promptly beyond the ground-effect band after liftoff.

The source explicitly links rapid vertical climb to rotor-RPM reduction and possible instability. Q182 tests insufficient RPM before liftoff; C005 tests an in-flight climb-rate decision after takeoff, so the decision boundary and mechanism application are distinct.

The current bank covers broad CRM resource use in Q088 and the five CRM skills in Q187, but not the source-defined TEM causal chain Threat -> Error -> UAS -> accident and the objective of breaking that chain using available resources before or after Error/UAS occurs.
